text:
There has been no post-Budget bump for the coalition government in a new poll.

The monthly Taxpayers' Union poll conducted by Curia - the traditional National Party pollster - has National, New Zealand First and ACT able to form a government - but only just.

The coalition would have a 62-seat majority - one more than the 61 seats required - which is the same result it received in this poll last month.

The Budget, which deliberately had no sugar hits for voters and instead concentrated on getting the books back into surplus, was held a week before Curia started polling.

Labour continues to be the most popular party, up 0.3 points to 32.2 percent, while National is in second place, up 0.1 points to 30.1 percent.

The Greens gained 1.8 points to 11.5 percent, New Zealand First dropped 0.3 points to 11.4 percent, and ACT gained 1.3 points to 7.8 percent.

On this poll, Te Pāti Māori drops 1 point to 3.1 percent and Opportunity Party sneaks slightly ahead to 3.2 percent - up 0.4 points on last month.

While the coalition would hold power with 62 seats if a government was formed today, the Opposition bloc would fall short on 58.

The preferred prime minister results have both Christopher Luxon and Chris Hipkins down.

Luxon dropped 2.7 points to 18.8 percent while Hipkins was down 1.9 points to 17.1 percent.

New Zealand First leader Winston Peters is up 1.2 points to 12.8; Green Party co-leader Chloe Swarbrick is on 8.1, up 2.7 points; and ACT leader David Seymour is up 2.4 points to 6.3 percent.

The poll was conducted by Curia Market Research Ltd for the NZ Taxpayers' Union. It is a random poll of 1000 adult New Zealanders and is weighted to the overall adult population. It was conducted by phone (landlines and mobile) and online between Thursday 4 June and Monday 8 June, 2026. It has a maximum margin of error of +/- 3.1 percent. The number of decided voters on the vote questions was 939. There were 46 (4.6 percent) undecided voters and 15 (1.5 percent) who refused the vote question.
